title: Health in depth
goal: Describe symptoms precisely, say how long they've lasted, mention allergies and conditions, get through a hospital visit and follow a pharmacist's instructions.
intro:
Unit 9 got you to the doctor; this unit gets you through the appointment. You'll describe symptoms precisely — what **burns** (पोल्छ), **itches** (चिलाउँछ) or **has swollen** (सुन्नियो), whether you're dizzy or throwing up — say **how long** it has been going on (**तीन दिनदेखि…**), mention allergies and conditions, and understand the doctor's and the pharmacist's instructions: **दिनको दुई पटक, खाना खाएपछि**.

Nepali health talk is full of English: **प्रेसर**, **सुगर**, **ग्यास्ट्रिक**, **एक्सरे**, **रिपोर्ट**. The grammar that holds it together is **-देखि** with the present tense for 'I have been … for', and the fixed patterns of medical instructions.

बान्ता हुनु / गर्नु 'to vomit'. Compare वाकवाकी 'nausea' (unit 9).
What Nepalis call almost any stomach complaint: ग्यास्ट्रिक भयो.
निद्रा लाग्यो 'I'm sleepy'; निद्रा लाग्दैन 'I can't sleep'.

How long has this been going on?

Don't take it on an empty stomach.

grammar.title: 'I have been … for three days': -देखि + present
grammar.body:
English says 'I **have been** coughing **for** three days'. Nepali says 'three days-**from** a cough is striking (me)': **तीन दिनदेखि खोकी लागिरहेको छ**. Two things change.

**1. 'For' and 'since' are both -देखि.** Add it to the length of time or to the starting point: **दुई हप्तादेखि** 'for two weeks', **हिजोदेखि** 'since yesterday', **बिहानदेखि** 'since this morning', **कहिलेदेखि?** 'since when? / for how long?'. Don't use **-को लागि** here — that is 'for' a period still ahead: तीन दिनको लागि औषधि 'medicine for three days'. And a course of treatment that runs *up to* a point uses **-सम्म**: पाँच दिनसम्म खानुहोस् 'take it for five days'.

**2. The verb is present, not past.** Use the continuous **-इरहेको छ** (or -दै छ) for something still going on: खोकी **लागिरहेको छ**, ज्वरो **आइरहेको छ**, पेट **दुखिरहेको छ**. For a state or a recurring symptom the simple present also works: हिजोदेखि टाउको **दुख्छ**. In the negative, use the perfect: दुई दिनदेखि निद्रा **लागेको छैन** 'I haven't slept for two days'.

**Another way: '…-एको X भयो'** — 'it has been X since…': ज्वरो **आएको** तीन दिन **भयो** 'it's been three days since the fever started'. This is the natural answer to **कति दिन भयो?** 'how long has it been?'. No -देखि in this pattern.

**Getting better or worse**: **-दै गएको छ** 'keeps …-ing': खोकी **बढ्दै गएको छ** 'the cough is getting worse'; ज्वरो **घट्दै छ** 'the fever is coming down'.

examples.en: I've had a cough for three days.
My stomach has been hurting since this morning.

examples.native: दुई दिनदेखि मलाई निद्रा लागेको छैन।
examples.roman: dui dindekhi malāi nidrā lāgeko chhaina.
examples.en: I haven't been able to sleep for two days.
How long have you had the fever?

examples.native: औषधि खान सुरु गरेको एक हप्ता भयो।
examples.roman: ausadhi khāna suru gareko ek haptā bhayo.
examples.en: I started the medicine a week ago.

grammar.title: Following instructions
grammar.body:
Doctors, pharmacists and medicine packets give instructions in a few fixed patterns.

**Do / don't: -नुहोस् / न-…-नुहोस्** (unit 11): दिनको दुई पटक **खानुहोस्**, चिसो पानी **नखानुहोस्**. On labels and prescriptions you'll see the bare infinitive in **-नु** used as a command: **दिनको तीन पटक खानु** 'to be taken three times a day'. Medicine is 'eaten' in Nepali, even syrup: औषधि **खानु**; ointment is 'applied': मलम **लगाउनु**.

**Must / mustn't**: **-नुपर्छ** 'you must', **-नुहुँदैन** 'you mustn't, it's not OK': आराम **गर्नुपर्छ**, रक्सी **खानुहुँदैन** 'no alcohol'. To ask: **-नुपर्छ?** 'do I have to?' and **-न हुन्छ?** 'is it OK to?': पानी पिउ**न हुन्छ**?

**When**: **खाना खाएपछि** 'after food' (-एपछि 'after doing'); **खाना खानुअघि** or **खानुभन्दा पहिले** 'before food' (-नुअघि 'before doing'); **खाली पेटमा** 'on an empty stomach'; **सुत्ने बेलामा** 'at bedtime'; **बिहान–बेलुका** 'morning and evening'.

**How often, how long**: **दिनको दुई पटक** 'twice a day', **हरेक आठ घण्टामा** 'every eight hours', **पाँच दिनसम्म** 'for five days', **सन्चो नभएसम्म** 'until you're better' (unit 30).

**Don't forget**: **-न नबिर्सनुहोस्**: औषधि **खान नबिर्सनुहोस्** 'don't forget to take your medicine'.

To check you've understood, repeat it back with the **-ने** form ('should I…?'): दिनको कति पटक **खाने**? खाना खाएपछि **खाने**, हो?

examples.native: सुत्ने बेलामा एक चम्चा सिरप खानुहोस्।
examples.roman: sutne belāmā ek chamchā sirap khānuhos.
examples.en: Take a spoonful of syrup at bedtime.
You have to take this medicine for five days.
You mustn't drink alcohol while taking the medicine.
Apply the ointment three times a day. (label)

dialogue.title: At the clinic
dialogue.setting: Ravi has had a fever and stomach trouble since coming back from a wedding in Chitwan. He goes to a clinic near Mahendrapul, Pokhara.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Have a seat. What's the problem?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: डाक्टरसाब, तीन दिनदेखि ज्वरो आइरहेको छ, अनि पेट पनि दुखिरहेको छ।
lines.roman: ḍākṭarsāb, tin dindekhi jwaro āiraheko chha, ani peṭ pani dukhiraheko chha.
lines.en: Doctor, I've had a fever for three days, and my stomach hurts too.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: हिजो दुई पटक भयो। केही खान मन लाग्दैन।
lines.roman: hijo dui paṭak bhayo. kehi khāna man lāgdaina.
lines.en: Twice yesterday. I don't feel like eating anything.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: चितवनमा एउटा बिहेमा गएको थिएँ… त्यहाँ धेरै खाएँ, हाहा।
lines.roman: Chitwanmā euṭā bihemā gaeko thieṃ… tyahāṃ dherai khāeṃ, hāhā.
lines.en: I went to a wedding in Chitwan… I ate a lot there, haha.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: बिहेको खानाले धेरैलाई यस्तै हुन्छ। कुनै औषधिको एलर्जी छ?
lines.roman: biheko khānāle dherailāi yastai hunchha. kunai ausadhiko elarji chha?
lines.en: Wedding food does this to a lot of people. Are you allergic to any medicine?

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ल, रगत र दिसा जाँच गरौँ। अनि यो औषधि दिनको तीन पटक खाना खाएपछि खानुहोस्।
lines.roman: la, ragat ra disā jāṃch garauṃ. ani yo ausadhi dinko tin paṭak khānā khāepachhi khānuhos.
lines.en: Right, let's do a blood and stool test. And take this medicine three times a day after food.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: पाँच दिनसम्म। सन्चो भए पनि बीचमा नछोड्नुहोस्। अनि धेरै पानी पिउनुहोस्।
lines.roman: pāṃch dinsamma. sancho bhae pani bichmā nachhoḍnuhos. ani dherai pāni piunuhos.
lines.en: Five days. Don't stop halfway even if you feel better. And drink plenty of water.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.en: And if the fever doesn't come down?

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: दुई दिनमा ज्वरो नघटे फेरि देखाउन आउनुहोस्।
lines.roman: dui dinmā jwaro naghaṭe pheri dekhāuna āunuhos.
lines.en: If it hasn't come down in two days, come back and see me.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.native: हुन्छ, धन्यवाद डाक्टरसाब। अब बिहेमा कम खान्छु!
lines.roman: hunchha, dhanyabād ḍākṭarsāb. aba bihemā kam khānchhu!
lines.en: OK, thank you, doctor. I'll eat less at weddings from now on!

culture:
For anything minor, most Nepalis go straight to the **मेडिकल** (pharmacy) on the corner, describe their symptoms and walk out with tablets; pharmacists dispense a lot without a prescription and often know their regulars. For a doctor, people say **डाक्टरलाई देखाउनु** 'to show (it) to the doctor'. Doctors are addressed as **डाक्टरसाब** or simply **डाक्टर**.

In big government hospitals (Bir, Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj, Western Regional in Pokhara) you start by buying an **ओपीडी टिकट** early in the morning, then queue for your **पालो**. Private hospitals and clinics take appointments by phone. A patient admitted to hospital is never left alone: a family member, the **कुरुवा**, stays day and night to fetch medicine, food and test results. The government health insurance scheme (**स्वास्थ्य बिमा**) covers many families for basic care.

You'll hear **ग्यास्ट्रिक** for almost any stomach complaint, **प्रेसर** and **सुगर** for blood pressure and diabetes, and **जीवनजल** for oral rehydration salts — the first thing anyone gives you for diarrhoea. Relatives will also recommend home remedies: hot water, **बेसार** (turmeric) in milk, and avoiding 'cold' foods like curd when you have a cough.

tip.title: Symptoms: what burns, itches or swells
tip.body:
- The body part is the subject: **टाउको दुख्यो**, **घाँटी पोल्छ** 'my throat burns', **हात सुन्नियो**, **छाला चिलाउँछ**.
- So the verb agrees with the body part: हात चिलाउँ**छ**, not चिलाउँछु.
- Sensations that 'strike' you take **मलाई**: मलाई **रिँगटा लाग्छ**, मलाई **बान्ता हुन्छ**.
tip.pattern: मेरो + body part + दुख्छ / पोल्छ  ·  मलाई + रिँगटा लाग्छ

sentences.en: My throat is burning.
My hand itches a lot.
Why has my foot swollen?
I felt dizzy when I stood up.

sentences.native: उसलाई राति दुई पटक बान्ता भयो।
sentences.roman: uslāi rāti dui paṭak bāntā bhayo.
sentences.en: She threw up twice in the night.
My gastritis is playing up — my stomach burns.
My eye is swollen.
Show me where the pain is.
What other symptoms do you have?

lessons.title: How long has this been going on?

tip.title: 'For three days': -देखि + present
tip.body:
- 'For' and 'since' are both **-देखि**: तीन दिन**देखि**, हिजो**देखि**, **कहिलेदेखि?**
- Keep the verb in the **present**: खोकी लागि**रहेको छ** 'I've been coughing'.
- Negative: दुई दिनदेखि निद्रा **लागेको छैन**.
- Not **-को लागि** — that's 'for' a time still ahead.

sentences.en: I've had a cough for two weeks.
I've had a headache non-stop since yesterday.
How long have you been feeling tired?

sentences.native: एक हप्तादेखि राति निद्रा लागेको छैन।
sentences.roman: ek haptādekhi rāti nidrā lāgeko chhaina.
sentences.en: I haven't slept properly for a week.
The pain's been getting worse since this morning.

sentences.native: तीन दिनदेखि केही खान मन लागेको छैन।
sentences.roman: tin dindekhi kehi khāna man lāgeko chhaina.
sentences.en: I haven't felt like eating anything for three days.

sentences.native: एक महिनादेखि लगातार काम गरिरहेको छु।
sentences.roman: ek mahinādekhi lagātār kām gariraheko chhu.
sentences.en: I've been working non-stop for a month.
The fever comes and goes.
The fever came down after I took the medicine.

tip.title: 'It's been X since…': -एको … भयो
tip.body:
- 'It's been three days since the fever started': ज्वरो **आएको** तीन दिन **भयो**.
- Ask: **कति दिन भयो?** 'how long has it been?'
- Verb-**एको** + time + **भयो** — and no -देखि in this pattern.

sentences.native: बुबालाई सुगर भएको पाँच वर्ष भयो।
sentences.roman: bubālāi sugar bhaeko pāṃch barsa bhayo.
sentences.en: Dad has had diabetes for five years.

sentences.native: प्रेसरको औषधि खान सुरु गरेको कति समय भयो?
sentences.roman: presarko ausadhi khāna suru gareko kati samaya bhayo?
sentences.en: How long have you been on blood-pressure medicine?
My skin has been swollen for two days.

sentences.native: यो एलर्जी भएको कति दिन भयो?
sentences.roman: yo elarji bhaeko kati din bhayo?
sentences.en: How long have you had this allergy?

sentences.native: अस्पताल गएको एक हप्ता भयो, अब सन्चो छ।
sentences.roman: aspatāl gaeko ek haptā bhayo, aba sancho chha.
sentences.en: It's been a week since I went to hospital, and I'm fine now.

sentences.native: औषधि खाएको दुई दिन भयो, तर अझै सन्चो भएन।
sentences.roman: ausadhi khāeko dui din bhayo, tara ajhai sancho bhaena.
sentences.en: I've been on the medicine for two days but I'm still not better.

sentences.native: मलाई धुलोको एलर्जी छ, काठमाडौंमा गाह्रो हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: malāi dhuloko elarji chha, Kāṭhmāḍauṃmā gāhro hunchha.
sentences.en: I'm allergic to dust, so Kathmandu is hard for me.

sentences.native: मेरो प्रेसर अलि बढेको छ रे।
sentences.roman: mero presar ali baḍheko chha re.
sentences.en: Apparently my blood pressure has gone up a bit.

sentences.native: हजुरआमालाई प्रेसर पनि छ, सुगर पनि।
sentences.roman: hajurāmālāi presar pani chha, sugar pani.
sentences.en: Grandma has both high blood pressure and diabetes.

tip.title: डाक्टरलाई देखाउनु
tip.body:
- 'To see a doctor' is **डाक्टरलाई देखाउनु** — lit. 'to show (it) to the doctor'. Don't mix up **देखाउनु** 'show' and **देख्नु** 'see'.
- In hospitals, first buy an **ओपीडी टिकट** (टिकट **काट्नु**), then wait for your **पालो** 'turn'.
- Ask what's needed with **-नुपर्छ?**

sentences.en: I'm going to see the doctor this evening.
Get a doctor to look at that injury, would you.

sentences.native: पहिले डाक्टरलाई देखाउनुहोस्, अनि मात्र औषधि खानुहोस्।
sentences.roman: pahile ḍākṭarlāi dekhāunuhos, ani mātra ausadhi khānuhos.
sentences.en: See a doctor first, and only then take medicine.
Come back and show me once the report is ready.

sentences.native: बिहान छ बजे ओपीडी टिकट काट्न लाइन बस्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: bihāna chha baje opiḍi ṭikaṭ kāṭna lāin basnuparchha.
sentences.en: You have to queue at six in the morning for an OPD ticket.
I've made an appointment with the doctor for tomorrow.
When will it be my turn?
Do you have insurance?

sentences.native: बिमा भए अस्पतालको बिल कम हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: bimā bhae aspatālko bil kam hunchha.
sentences.en: If you're insured, the hospital bill is lower.

tip.title: Must and mustn't
tip.body:
- **-नुपर्छ** 'you must': रगत जाँच **गर्नुपर्छ**.
- **-नुहुँदैन** 'you mustn't': केही **खानुहुँदैन**.
- Asking: **-नुपर्छ?** 'do I have to?' · **-न हुन्छ?** 'is it OK to?': पानी पिउ**न हुन्छ**?

sentences.en: You need to have a blood test tomorrow morning.
You mustn't eat anything before giving blood.
You need a urine and a blood test.
Do I need an X-ray of my foot?
Is it OK to drink water before the X-ray?

sentences.native: भर्ना भएपछि घरबाट कसैले साथमा बस्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: bharnā bhaepachhi gharbāṭa kasaile sāthmā basnuparchha.
sentences.en: Once a patient is admitted, someone from the family has to stay with them.
I'm scared of injections!
Grandfather has been admitted to hospital.
The spot where I had the injection has swollen a bit.

tip.title: Medicine instructions
tip.body:
- When: **खाना खाएपछि** 'after food', **खाना खानुअघि** 'before food', **खाली पेटमा**, **सुत्ने बेलामा**.
- How often: **दिनको दुई पटक**, **हरेक आठ घण्टामा**; how long: **पाँच दिनसम्म**.
- Labels use the bare **-नु** as a command: दिनको तीन पटक **खानु**.
- Check back with **-ने?**: कति पटक **खाने**?
tip.pattern: दिनको X पटक + खाना खाएपछि + खानुहोस्

sentences.native: यो चक्की दिनको दुई पटक खानुहोस्।
sentences.roman: yo chakki dinko dui paṭak khānuhos.
sentences.en: Take this tablet twice a day.
Take the syrup before food.
Put this ointment on at bedtime.

sentences.native: हरेक आठ घण्टामा एउटा चक्की खानु।
sentences.roman: harek āṭh ghanṭāmā euṭā chakki khānu.
sentences.en: Take one tablet every eight hours. (label)
Take this syrup for five days.

sentences.native: दाइ, यो सिरप खाना खाएपछि खाने, हो?
sentences.roman: dāi, yo sirap khānā khāepachhi khāne, ho?
sentences.en: Dai, I take this syrup after food, right?

sentences.native: यो औषधि खाँदा निद्रा लाग्छ, गाडी नचलाउनुहोस्।
sentences.roman: yo ausadhi khāṃdā nidrā lāgchha, gāḍi nachalāunuhos.
sentences.en: This medicine makes you drowsy — don't drive.
